visual_action: A split-screen style video. The first half, in black and white and labeled "UNDER BIDEN:", shows several clips of large groups of people, presumably migrants, walking in a line and crossing a body of water or ditch near a border fence with barbed wire. The second half, in color and labeled "UNDER TRUMP", is a montage of B-roll showing a helicopter flying over a border wall, a U.S. Border Patrol agent in tactical gear, a patrol boat speeding on water, an off-road vehicle driving fast and kicking up dust, and an aerial shot of a long border wall in the desert. The video concludes with "THE WHITE HOUSE" logo over a black and white shot of the building.

cast.name: Joe Biden
cast.evidence: The text "UNDER BIDEN:" appears on screen over the first set of clips.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: The text "UNDER TRUMP" appears on screen over the second set of clips.

cast.name: U.S. Border Patrol
cast.evidence: An agent is shown with a "U.S. BORDER PATROL" patch on his uniform, and their vehicles (helicopter, boat) are featured.

cast.name: The White House
cast.evidence: The video ends with a logo that says "THE WHITE HOUSE" and is posted by the @whitehouse account.

spoken_summary: The video's audio has two distinct parts. The first few seconds, over the "Biden" section, consist of a jarring, repetitive, high-pitched electronic sound effect. This is immediately followed by a loud, aggressive rock song with a male voice shouting lyrics like "Fucking hell yeah, brother."
audio_music: The video begins with a jarring, rapid electronic sound effect for approximately 3 seconds to create a chaotic mood. It then abruptly switches to the high-energy, aggressive rock track "Hell Yeah Brother" by Jeris Johnson for the remainder of the video, creating a powerful and hype-filled atmosphere.
editing_pacing: The video uses fast-paced cuts in a montage format to create a stark contrast between two distinct sections.
emotions_signaled: Anxiety/Chaos (evoked by grainy, black-and-white footage of migrants and jarring sound under 'Biden')
Pride/Strength/Excitement (evoked by high-energy montage of Border Patrol equipment and personnel set to aggressive rock music under 'Trump')
cultural_references: The song 'Hell Yeah Brother' by Jeris Johnson.
The phrase 'Hell yeah, brother' is a meme associated with a particular hyper-masculine, enthusiastic online subculture.
central_claim: The border was chaotic and overrun with migrants under President Biden, whereas it was secure and powerfully patrolled under President Trump.
intended_effect: To create anxiety about border security under Biden and generate support for Trump's policies by portraying them as strong and effective.
uncertainty_flags: The provenance and dates of the footage used to represent the 'Biden' and 'Trump' eras are unstated and unverified within the video.
